assignment: Apply bounded-width/high-variance results to the exact width-three target and derive the remaining exceptional-case requirement with constants/hypotheses explicit.

partner_result_consumed.applied: endpoint pinned-mass plus rank-variance mechanism giving E[J^2]<585/64 and a quantitative shallow-cut tail without replacing the projected law by uniform

additional_dependency.applied: exact first-element insertion law dmu/dnu=(kappa+1)/E_nu[kappa+1], where nu is genuinely uniform on L(P\{c})

essential_step: For the first strong-majority element c, let Q=P\{c}, let nu be uniform on L(Q), kappa the initial incomparability-ideal prefix length, W=kappa+1, and mu the exact projection of uniform L(P), so dmu/dnu=W/E_nu W. If J=rank(c)-1 then Pr(J=0)>4/9 and Var(J)<65/16 imply E[J^2]<585/64. Conditional on kappa under the actual projected law, J is uniform on {0,...,kappa}, hence E_mu[kappa(2kappa+1)]<1755/32. Therefore mu(kappa>=47)<351/28576<1/81, so more than 80/81 of the actual projected mass has W<=47. Size-bias inversion also gives E_nu[kappa(kappa+1)(2kappa+1)]<15795/128 and nu(kappa>=17)<351/30464<1/81. Thus the unbounded-weight transfer problem reduces to a 47-bounded core plus <1/81 projected tail, under the actual induced law rather than a uniform surrogate.
remaining_requirement: BW47-WICSL: on G={kappa<=46}, with mu_G the exact (kappa+1)-tilt of nu conditioned on G and all no-balanced/endpoint-blocker constraints retained, find an incomparable pair with mu_G ordering probability in [28/81,53/81]. This would transfer to [1/3,2/3] under full mu because mu(G^c)<1/81.
